title: Fitra, hanif and Islam are one thing
text: The fitra of 30:30 is Islam itself; ḥanīfan and fiṭrata llāh name the same thing.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Inborn knowledge of God is more precise than the greatest theologian's
text: Nothing correct a theologian could say cannot be dug out of oneself.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Lā tabdīl: the fitra can be damaged but never replaced
text: So it is always recoverable; tabdīl (replacement) is excluded, taghyīr (change) is not.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: All misguidance comes from society, not from human nature
text: Parents and society corrupt; the self is not a source of going astray.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Everyone has the fitra completely and equally
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: abu-hurayra affirms identity
text: Recites 30:30 immediately after 'every child is born on the fitra'.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: muadh affirms identity
text: 'Sincerity (ikhlas) is the fitra', quoting 30:30; ʿUmar answered 'you spoke truly'.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: umar affirms identity
text: Approved Muʿadh's answer that sincerity is the fitra.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ikrima affirms identity
text: The fitra of God is the religion of God.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: alusi qualifies identity
text: Badal (ḥanīfan = fiṭrata llāh) is only a permissible parsing; the more natural reading is ighrāʾ, 'hold fast to the fitra'. The identity rests on the Companions, not the syntax.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: quran rejects innate-knowledge
text: 'God brought you out of your mothers' wombs knowing nothing' (16:78); 'you did not know what the Book was, nor faith' (42:52).
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ibn-abd-al-barr rejects innate-knowledge
text: That a child is born knowing God 'is what observation and reason belie'; the most correct reading is soundness and uprightness. Yet he grants, as the consensus of Ahl al-Sunna, an inborn pull toward a Creator once reason matures.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ibn-taymiyya qualifies innate-knowledge
text: The fitra contains acknowledging and loving the Creator, as a newborn desires the milk that suits it; but it is not knowledge of the religion at birth; it develops, and messengers complete it.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ghazali qualifies innate-knowledge
text: Faith lies hidden in the soul as a nearby readiness, recovered by remembering; but no one draws near to God by instinct alone, only through acquired knowledge.

cites.loc: Ihyaʾ, pp. 168, 497 (study's page refs; record ids pending)

by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ibn-arabi affirms innate-knowledge
text: An infant's faith is 'more complete than an adult's, without doubt'; the spirit is created knowing and believing in God's oneness.

cites.loc: al-Futuhat, Shamela ed. p. 670 (record id pending)

by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ibn-al-qayyim affirms la-tabdil
text: What people are born upon is God's creation, which no one but He could replace, and He does not; unlike exchanging unbelief for faith, which happens often.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: mujahid rejects la-tabdil
text: 'No changing God's creation' means God's religion: a command not to change it, not a statement that it cannot be replaced.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: tabari rejects la-tabdil
text: Reads lā tabdīl as no taghyīr of God's religion, a prohibition; he does not distinguish tabdīl from taghyīr.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: quran rejects misguidance-external
text: 'He inspired it with its wickedness and its piety' (91:8); 'the self commands evil' (12:53): a source of going astray within.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: ibn-arabi rejects misguidance-external
text: 'Man's disobedience comes from what he was created upon; his obedience from what he was created for.'

cites.loc: al-Futuhat, Shamela ed. p. 74 (record id pending)

by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: rumi qualifies equal
text: Souls who heard Alast forget it wholly, partly or not at all, 'according to their rank and essence'.

cites.loc: Fihi ma fihi, ch. 14 (record id pending)

title: ghazali qualifies equal
text: Some are born with perfect character and need no teaching.

title: Verdict: identity
text: Backed by the Companions and Followers; the grammar argument is weaker than the inference.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Verdict: innate-knowledge
text: The leaning toward the Creator is agreed (even Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr calls it the consensus of Ahl al-Sunna); inborn knowledge of the details is rejected by the Qur'an, Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr and Ibn Taymiyya; only Ibn ʿArabi goes as far as the lecturer.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Verdict: la-tabdil
text: Holds as Ibn al-Qayyim's reading; al-Tabari, Mujahid and others read the phrase as a prohibition, so the distinction is a choice between readings, not a given.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Verdict: misguidance-external
text: The Qur'an and Ibn ʿArabi place a second source within the self; the lecturer's own remedy (purifying the heart) assumes it.
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Verdict: equal
text: All have the fitra, but its strength differs (Rumi, al-Ghazali).
by: Claude, from two studies of the fitra lecture (2026-10-01), entered in v41

title: Does the Jalasa's Ibn ʿArabi side with the lecturer on infant faith?
text: He is the one master who affirms inborn faith beyond the lecturer; the full passages should be read in context.
